headline: Pakistan Reaches 28.2 Million Children in Major Polio Campaign
meta_description: Pakistan's weeklong polio vaccination drive reached over 28 million children with help from 273,000 frontline health workers across the country.
summary_short: Pakistan's health workers vaccinated more than 28 million children against polio in a single week, deploying 273,000 frontline staff across the nation.
body:
Over 28.2 million children received polio vaccine drops during Pakistan's weeklong immunization campaign from September 21 to 27, marking a major push in the country's ongoing effort to eliminate the disease.

The scale of the operation underscores the logistical challenge of reaching vulnerable populations. Frontline health workers—273,000 strong—visited homes and communities throughout Pakistan, bringing vaccination directly to children rather than waiting for families to come to clinics.

Polio remains a critical public health priority in Pakistan, one of the few countries where the virus still circulates. Mass campaigns like this one represent the frontline defense against a disease that can cause permanent paralysis in children.
quick_facts: 28.2 million children vaccinated in Pakistan, September 21–27
273,000 frontline workers deployed across the country
Seven-day vaccination campaign targeting polio elimination
